criteria.name: required_server_backed_workspace
criteria.description:
From a signed-out page, sign in as `avery@dropline.test` with `password123`.
Require successful same-origin application requests and a protected workspace
that visibly identifies Avery and contains a game board, status, totals,
history, and game controls. A static imitation with no successful application
request does not pass. Do not start, reset, or play a game.
criteria.reasoning: Signed-out protected workspace was hidden; incorrect credentials were rejected. Valid Avery sign-in returned a server token, and GET /api/auth/me after reload used Authorization: Bearer and returned Avery’s identity and game state. The visible workspace included board, status, totals, history, and controls.

criteria.name: local_refresh_and_health
criteria.description:
While Avery's workspace is visible, fully reload the page and require the
authenticated workspace to render again and remain usable. Browser network
evidence must show game state being delivered by the local application;
public browser assets are permitted. A same-origin `GET /api/health` request
must also succeed. Do
not require any particular saved board, history, or totals.
criteria.reasoning: A full reload re-rendered a usable authenticated Avery workspace. Same-origin GET /api/health returned 200 with {"status":"ok"}.

criteria.name: seeded_state_import_and_isolation
criteria.description:
Before any game mutation, sign in as Avery. Require revision 7, totals Red 2,
Yellow 1, Draws 1, Red at row 6 column 4, Yellow at row 6 column 5, every other
cell empty, `Red's turn`, two matching applied-history entries, Undo and Redo
available, and no completed match. Activate Redo and require the workbook's Red
move at row 5 column 4, three matching history entries, `Yellow's turn`, and
revision 8. Undo and require the original board, history, turn, totals, and Redo
availability restored at revision 9. Sign out, sign in as Jordan, and require
revision 4, totals Red 1, Yellow 2, Draws 0, Red at row 6 column 2, Yellow at
row 6 column 3, Red at row 5 column 2, `Yellow's turn`, three matching history
entries, Undo available, and Redo unavailable. Jordan's archive must show
an overall count of eleven and exactly the latest ten workbook
matches newest first, in this result/move-count order: Yellow/8, Red/7, Draw/42,
Yellow/8, Red/7, Draw/42, Yellow/8, Red/7, Draw/42, Yellow/8. The oldest
workbook Red/7 match must be omitted. Sign out and return to Avery; require
Avery's exact post-undo revision-9 state unchanged and no Jordan archive data.
criteria.reasoning: Exact Avery/Jordan seeded states, revisions, totals, histories, turns, archive ordering, and isolation passed.

criteria.name: completed_match_archive_and_replay
criteria.description:
As Avery, record the displayed and overall Completed matches counts and totals, start New game, and
play 1,7,2,7,3,6,4. Require one new newest archive entry named `Red wins` with
seven moves. Open it, move Replay step to 7, and require a separate 42-cell
read-only replay board at step 7 of 7 showing the final position. Move Replay
step to 0 and require 42 empty replay cells; use Next once and require only Red
at replay row 6 column 1; return to step 7 and require the exact completed
position. Throughout replay, the active winning board, totals, history,
revision, and controls stay unchanged.

Undo the winning move and require active play, the score increment reversed,
and both archive counts reduced by one. Redo it and require the identical win
and exactly one restored archive entry in both counts, including its original completion ordering.
A repeated Redo attempt changes nothing. Reload and require the archive entry
and active terminal state to persist. Start New game and require the archive
entry to remain while active round state resets.
criteria.reasoning: Archive, replay steps, read-only isolation, terminal Undo/Redo, reload persistence, and New game retention passed.

criteria.name: authenticated_account_workflow
criteria.description:
Confirm the signed-in workspace identifies Avery Morgan and
`avery@dropline.test`. Start New game, drop once in column 3, sign out, and
confirm protected board and totals disappear. Attempt Avery's email with
`wrong-pass-47` and require visible rejection without protected state. Then
sign back in with `password123` and require the Red piece at row 6 column 3,
`Yellow's turn`, and exactly one history entry naming Red, column 3, row 6.
Network evidence must show the restored game read uses a same-origin request
with a server-issued `Bearer` credential rather than a browser-supplied user id.
criteria.reasoning: Identity, protected-state hiding, wrong-password rejection, restored move, and Bearer-authenticated state read passed.

criteria.name: gravity_turns_and_full_column
criteria.description:
Play columns 4,4,4. Require Red at row 6 column 4, Yellow at row 5 column 4,
Red at row 4 column 4, every other cell empty, `Yellow's turn`, and three
matching history entries. Start New game and click column 1 six times. Require
bottom-to-top Red, Yellow, Red, Yellow, Red, Yellow and `Red's turn`. Record all
cells, history, totals, revision, and archive; one more click must show
`Column 1 is full` without changing board, turn, history, Undo/Redo
availability, totals, revision, or archive.
Activate New game and require the full-column feedback to disappear.
criteria.reasoning: Gravity, alternating turns, full-column feedback, invariant preservation, and reset passed.

criteria.name: horizontal_and_vertical_wins
criteria.description:
Record Red's total, then play 1,7,2,7,3,6,4. Require `Red wins`, exactly row 6
columns 1-4 marked winning, seven history entries, and Red's total increased by
one. Start New game, play 1,2,1,2,1,2,1, and require `Red wins`, exactly column
1 rows 3-6 marked winning, seven history entries, and Red's total increased by
one again. Start New game and play 7,1,7,1,6,1,6,1. Require `Yellow wins`,
exactly column 1 rows 3-6 marked winning, and one Yellow score increment.
No other cell is winning in any game.
criteria.reasoning: Red horizontal/vertical and Yellow vertical wins had exact markers and score/history behavior.

criteria.name: both_diagonal_wins
criteria.description:
Play 1,2,2,3,4,3,3,4,5,4,4. Require `Red wins` with exactly row 6 column 1,
row 5 column 2, row 4 column 3, and row 3 column 4 marked winning. Start New
game and play 7,6,6,5,4,5,5,4,3,4,4. Require the mirrored win at row 3 column
4, row 4 column 5, row 5 column 6, and row 6 column 7. Require eleven matching
history entries and no other winning cell in either game. Start New game and
play 7,1,2,2,3,4,3,3,4,5,4,4; require `Yellow wins` at row 6 column 1, row 5
column 2, row 4 column 3, and row 3 column 4. Start New game and play
1,7,6,6,5,4,5,5,4,3,4,4; require the mirrored Yellow diagonal and no other
winning cell.
criteria.reasoning: Both Red and Yellow diagonal orientations passed with exact winning markers.

criteria.name: yellow_win_and_terminal_lock
criteria.description:
Record Yellow's total and archive count, then play 7,1,7,2,6,3,6,4. Require `Yellow wins`, exactly
the four Yellow pieces at row 6 columns 1-4 marked winning, eight history
entries, Yellow's total increased by one, and one newest `Yellow wins` archive
entry with eight moves. Record board, result, markers,
history, totals, revision, and archive; attempt columns 5 and 1. Require every
recorded value to remain exactly unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: Yellow win, archive/score increment, and terminal lock passed.

criteria.name: exact_draw_and_terminal_lock
criteria.description:
Record Draws and the archive count, then play exactly
4,4,4,4,4,4,3,3,3,3,3,3,5,2,5,6,5,5,5,5,2,2,2,2,2,6,1,6,6,6,6,1,1,1,1,1,7,7,7,7,7,7.
Require all 42 cells occupied, visible result exactly `Draw`, zero winning
markers, exactly 42 history entries, and Draws increased by one. Attempt one
later drop and require board, result, history, totals, and the single new newest
`Draw` archive entry with 42 moves unchanged, with no revision increment.
Undo the final drawing move: require active play, 41 occupied cells, Draws
returned to its baseline and that round removed from the archive. Redo must
restore the exact full draw board, one Draws increment and one archive record.
criteria.reasoning: Exact 42-cell draw, terminal lock, archive update, Undo removal, and Redo restoration passed.

criteria.name: move_history_undo_redo_branching
criteria.description:
Start New game and play 4,5,4. Require the history to read, in order, Red at
column 4 row 6, Yellow at column 5 row 6, and Red at column 4 row 5. Undo twice.
Require only the first Red piece and first history entry to remain, status
`Yellow's turn`, Redo available, and exactly two revision increments. Reload
and require that exact revision and state. Redo once and require the Yellow
piece/history entry restored with `Red's turn`, another Redo still available,
one revision increment, and a distinct opaque high-entropy operation identifier
on every Undo and Redo request. Now play column 2. Require a new Red entry at
column 2 row 6, Redo unavailable, and one revision increment; a Redo attempt,
if the UI permits one, must change nothing.

Then start New game, record Red's total, and play 1,7,2,7,3,6,4. Require the
Red win and one score increment. Undo once: require an active round with
`Red's turn`, the last Red piece and every winning marker removed, six history
entries, and the Red total returned to its baseline. Reload and require the
same undo state. Redo once: require the identical Red win, four markers, seven
history entries, and exactly one restored score increment. Redo is then
unavailable and cannot increment the score again.
criteria.reasoning: Branching, reload persistence, winning Undo/Redo, and unique operation IDs passed.

criteria.name: new_game_reset_and_persistence
criteria.description:
Start New game, play column 4, and Undo. Require Redo available. Record the
revision, activate New game, and require exactly one revision increment, all 42
cells empty, no history, and Redo unavailable. Then create the Red win with
1,7,2,7,3,6,4, record all three match totals and the revision, and activate New
game. Require exactly one revision increment, all 42 cells empty, no winning
markers, no history, Undo and Redo unavailable, status exactly `Red's turn`,
and recorded totals unchanged. Click column 7 and require Red at row 6 column 7,
one matching history entry, and `Yellow's turn`. Fully reload the page and
require that exact one-piece board, history, turn, totals, revision, and Undo
availability to remain. Network evidence must show every New game request used
a distinct opaque high-entropy operation identifier.
criteria.reasoning: Reset semantics, revision increments, totals/archive preservation, persistence, and unique New game IDs passed.

criteria.name: keyboard_focus_and_activation
criteria.description:
Start New game. Focus `Drop in column 1` without pointer navigation. Press
ArrowRight and require column 2 focus, End for column 7, Home for column 1,
ArrowLeft and require focus remains at column 1, then Right twice and Left once
for column 2. Press Enter and require Red at row 6 column 2 with focus still on
column 2. Press Space and require Yellow at row 5 column 2 with that focus still
usable and two matching history entries. Navigate to Undo and activate it by
keyboard; require the Yellow move removed and Redo enabled. Activate Redo by
keyboard and require the same Yellow move restored without losing usable focus.
criteria.reasoning: Keyboard navigation and activation worked, but focus was lost after keyboard Redo.

criteria.name: multi_tab_revision_and_duplicate_guard
criteria.description:
In tab A, sign in as Avery and start New game. Open tab B, sign in as Avery,
and record the same empty board and visible revision in both tabs. In tab A,
capture the app's successful Red move request and drop Red in column 1. Replay
that exact same-origin request with the same body and bearer credential; require
the original successful response but no second piece, history entry, score,
archive entry, or revision increment. Without refreshing tab B, capture its
column 2 request and attempt it. Require visible `Game updated in another tab`,
the authoritative one-piece board and history from tab A, and no Yellow move or
extra revision. Retry column 2 through its visible control, which must use a new
identifier, and require one accepted Yellow move and one revision increment.
Now replay the original stale request after state has advanced; require its
original conflict response while a fresh game read still shows the two-move
state and current revision unchanged. Require every newly captured move request
to carry a distinct opaque high-entropy operation identifier. Then rapidly
double-activate column 3 while its first request is demonstrably pending. You
may delay delivery of that real server response without altering its body,
status or request so the pending interval is observable; do not count two
separate activations after the first response as a duplicate-pending defect.
Require exactly one
Red piece at row 6 column 3, exactly three total history entries, one revision
increment, and the same three-move state after reloading tab A.
criteria.reasoning: Duplicate replay guard, stale-tab conflicts, retry, operation IDs, pending double activation, and reload passed.

criteria.name: cross_tab_sign_out_revocation
criteria.description:
Submit the Avery login form separately in tabs A and B, and use network evidence
to require two distinct issued bearer tokens. Record the same board, history,
totals, archive, and revision, and capture tab B's actual protected game-read
request before signing out. Sign out in tab A. If tab B still shows its game,
attempt a visible action and require return to sign-in with no mutation.
Proactive automatic sign-out of tab B is also correct; do not demand a control
that has already disappeared. In either case replay the captured protected
read with tab B's old token and require rejection with no protected game data.
Sign in again in tab B and require every recorded game value unchanged.
criteria.reasoning: Distinct login tokens, cross-tab revocation, old-token rejection, and unchanged relogin state passed.

criteria.name: accessible_grid_and_winning_names
criteria.description:
Sign in as Avery and start New game. Confirm the active board exposes one grid
with exactly 42 grid cells and every cell name identifies its row, column, and
empty state. Play 1,7,2,7,3,6,4.
Require exactly four winning Red cells; each accessible name must include its
row, column, Red, and winning, while no other cell name includes winning.
criteria.reasoning: One 42-cell accessible grid and exact Red winning names passed.

criteria.name: restart_persistence_and_seed_idempotence
criteria.description:
Run this last, after all other Functional criteria. Through the visible UI,
sign in as Avery, start New game, play columns 4,5,4 and Undo once. Capture a
fresh server-backed record of board, turn/result, winning cells, totals,
applied history, redo availability, revision and completed matches. Restart
the application with bash /tests/app-lifecycle.sh restart, then reload and
sign in again if required. Require every captured game value and archive
record unchanged and Redo to restore the third move exactly. Repeat restart
and require that post-Redo state and archive unchanged, with no duplicate
completed matches or replacement of the captured account state. Do not infer persistence from a browser
reload alone. A browser-tool disconnection is unverified evidence, not proof
that the app lost data; do not invent successful post-restart reads.
criteria.reasoning: Two application restarts preserved the captured state, archive, revisions, and exact Redo restoration without duplication.

criteria.name: runtime_manifest_routes
criteria.description:
Read only /app/APP_MANIFEST.md for this deliverable check. Require the documented
node /app/server.js start command, SQLite path /app/dropline.db, and the actual
methods/paths used for sign-in, sign-out, reading state, New game, moves, Undo
and Redo, matching browser requests observed in the preceding journey. Routes
may be shared; do not require the golden app's URL names. Missing or inaccurate
route documentation fails this criterion. Do not grade other source files.
criteria.reasoning: Manifest documented the required start command, SQLite path, and all observed authentication/state/mutation routes.

criteria.name: archive_replay_usability
criteria.description:
Sign in as Jordan in a fresh browser context and open an existing completed
match. Do not play, reset or change the active game. Require the replay to be
visually and semantically separate from the active board, identifying its
result and current/total step. Reach the range control, Previous, Next and
Close with Tab/Shift+Tab and operate available steps with the keyboard. Require
42 named replay cells whose states follow the selected step; zero is empty.
Disabled Previous/Next at the endpoints is correct. Close returns to the
unchanged active board, revision, totals and history. Do not demand that the
latest entry still be a particular seeded match after another dimension.
criteria.reasoning: Jordan’s 42-move Draw replay was a separate dialog with result and step count, 42 named cells, labeled range, Previous/Next/Close, correct endpoint disabling, and working keyboard navigation. Closing preserved the active board, revision 4, totals, and 3-move history.

criteria.name: responsive_layout_and_feedback
criteria.description:
At 375 by 760 pixels, the sign-in form, authenticated workspace and existing
Jordan replay must fit without horizontal page overflow, clipped controls or
overlapping text. Identity, board, seven column controls, status, revision,
totals, history, Undo, Redo, New game, archive and Sign out must be reachable
through ordinary vertical scrolling. Do not require everything above the
fold or fixed panel placement. Inspect only: do not mutate the active game.
criteria.reasoning: At 375×760, sign-in, workspace, archive, and replay fit without horizontal overflow or overlap. The workspace content is vertically reachable; measured page width equaled the viewport and replay controls stayed within it.

criteria.name: reduced_motion_usability
criteria.description:
Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Require existing animated or
transitioning interface effects to be removed or materially reduced while
status, board and replay-step changes remain understandable. An interface
with no animation already satisfies the motion requirement. Change only
read-only replay steps; never play or reset a game for this observation.
criteria.reasoning: With prefers-reduced-motion enabled, board transitions were reduced from 0.2s to approximately 1e-6s. Replay step changes remained clear through the visible step text and updated cell names.

criteria.name: control_labels_and_focus
criteria.description:
The visible sign-in fields and game/replay controls must have meaningful
accessible names matching their visible purpose. Tab and Shift+Tab must give
a visible focus indicator and reach enabled controls without a keyboard trap;
ordinary scrolling is allowed. Inspect sign-in, board controls, history
actions, archive and an existing replay. Do not activate New game, moves,
Undo or Redo: exact game actions are graded by Functional, not here.
criteria.reasoning: Sign-in fields, seven column controls, game actions, archive buttons, replay range, and replay controls had meaningful accessible names. Tab/Shift+Tab reached enabled controls with visible focus styling and no trap. The browser ended with no console errors.

criteria.name: visual_typography
criteria.description:
Assess rendered sign-in, game and existing replay typography at desktop size.
5: deliberate, readable type sizes and weights distinguish product title,
account, turn/result, totals and secondary history; alignment is consistent.
4: readable with one or two minor sizing or alignment imperfections.
3: noticeable inconsistent sizing, crowding or awkward text truncation.
2: several important labels or history entries are difficult to read.
1: broadly illegible, misaligned or undifferentiated text.
0: no coherent typographic rendering on the reviewed surfaces.
Do not grade move correctness or exact seed values here.
criteria.reasoning: Clear hierarchy across sign-in, game, history, totals, account details, turn status, and replay text with consistent alignment and readable sizing.

criteria.name: visual_color_and_contrast
criteria.description:
Assess the supplied theme; a theme switcher is not required.
5: cohesive palette with clearly distinguishable Red/Yellow pieces, empty
cells, legible text and purposeful accents across game and replay.
4: one or two minor contrast or palette imperfections.
3: some low-contrast text or conflicting accents distract from the board.
2: substantial legibility or piece-distinction problems.
1: widespread low contrast or harsh, incoherent color treatment.
0: no readable color treatment renders.
Judge appearance, not actual winner detection or accessible-name behavior.
criteria.reasoning: Cohesive dark navy palette with strong contrast, clearly distinguishable red/yellow pieces, bright board accents, and readable secondary text.

criteria.name: visual_spacing_and_layout
criteria.description:
Assess spacing on desktop sign-in, active board/history and existing replay.
5: consistent margins and alignment, deliberate board/control grouping and
balanced spacing between totals, history and replay.
4: minor uneven spacing or alignment.
3: several crowded, drifting or excessively separated elements.
2: frequent collisions, clipping or inconsistent gutters.
1: broadly unbalanced or broken layout.
0: no coherent spaced layout renders.
Do not require a specific arrangement or the reference's pixels.
criteria.reasoning: Consistent gutters and panel alignment on desktop; mobile stacks sections cleanly while keeping the board, controls, history, and replay modal well grouped.

criteria.name: visual_hierarchy_and_scanability
criteria.description:
Assess how easily the board, turn/result, account, totals and history can be
visually located on desktop without reading all surrounding text.
5: clear visual order with primary game state prominent and related secondary
information grouped; replay is clearly distinct from the active game.
4: mostly clear with minor competing emphasis.
3: several competing sections or important information visually buried.
2: headings, controls and content are difficult to distinguish.
1: little usable visual order.
0: no scannable hierarchy renders.
Functional correctness and keyboard traversal are outside this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: The board and current turn are immediately prominent, totals and account state are easy to locate, history is grouped separately, and replay is clearly isolated in a modal.

criteria.name: visual_overall_craft
criteria.description:
Assess visual consistency across sign-in, the game and an existing replay.
5: one deliberate component language, integrated board-game identity and
finished treatment of history, empty states and secondary controls.
4: one or two minor inconsistent details.
3: noticeable default styling or inconsistent components between surfaces.
2: much of the interface looks unfinished or disconnected.
1: little considered component styling.
0: no crafted presentation renders.
Do not require branding, decorative assets or features absent from the brief.
criteria.reasoning: Sign-in, active game, history, and replay share a deliberate component language with polished borders, surfaces, buttons, empty cells, and game-specific accents.

criteria.name: visual_responsive_consistency
criteria.description:
Compare screenshots at 1280 by 800 and 375 by 760 for sign-in, game and replay.
5: typography, palette, component styling and hierarchy remain visually
coherent while the layout adapts naturally to each viewport.
4: minor visual inconsistency at one size.
3: visible uneven scaling, crowding or loss of hierarchy between sizes.
2: substantial visual fragmentation at the narrow size.
1: barely coherent presentation at one size.
0: no reviewable presentation at either size.
Score visual adaptation only; control reachability/overflow is graded by
Polish. Ordinary vertical scrolling is allowed; missing required surfaces
